tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> collides head on elastically with a stationary body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>. After collision, the smaller body reverses its direction of motion and moves with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The initial speed of the smaller body before collision is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

solution.text:
Let u1 be the initial speed of the smaller body before collision. 

Let v be the final speed of the bigger body after collision.

Applying conservation of linear momentum,

1×u1+0=-2+3v⇒u1=-2+3v    ...1 

We know, coefficient of restitution for elastic perfectly collision is 1.

 ⇒1=v+2u1⇒v+2=u1    ...2 

Equating 1 and 2, we have

u1=4 m s-1.
